0466f18e:
Say what is built and what is only intended

The previous change made the tree tell the truth about what code is
there. This one is about what the code DOES, which is smaller and
harder: the README described three product claims in the present tense,
and one of them was half built while two did not exist.

Each claim now carries the state it is actually in and the commands it
rests on, and `scripts/release_check.py` resolves those command names
against the parser in both directions: a block that says "built" while
naming a command nobody wrote fails, and so does a command that works
while no block claims it.

The integrations that could not run are gone rather than shipped.
08eb233e:
Delete every module no command can reach, and describe what is left

Half this repository could not be reached from any command, and the front
page described the product of six months ago. Both are measurable, so
both were measured before anything was deleted.

An AST import walk from `cli.py`, `mcp.py` and `__main__.py` reached 26
of 55 modules. Twenty-nine modules and 8,989 lines had no route to any
command: `state/` had no importer at all, `conformance/` had three and
all three were themselves unreachable, and `coverage.py` was alive only
through a writing half of `attest/dsse.py` that no command called.

`tests/test_reachability.py` is the rule as a test, computed through
functions rather than through module-level imports.
bf349a98:
DEF-115: a receipt from a workspace referenced no evidence

`assurance-receipt/v2` publishes an `evidence` array so a receipt can
name the observations it rested on. The lookup matched each record's
subject against the subject's handle and against its digest, and nothing
is ever filed under either: the producers file per-artifact records under
an id derived from the artifact's URI. The two sets never intersected.

Silent in the worst way. `receipt issue --state` exited 0 and signed a
valid document every time, with the field absent, indistinguishable from
a workspace that had recorded nothing.

The lookup goes through `state.record.resolve` now, the same function the
producers use, so the two ends agree by construction.
18837068:
Make the package buildable again, and upload our own SARIF

`make package` had been failing on every run since the pivot: the list of
resources it asserts named five files that went with the model scanner,
and the CI job that builds the same distributions asserted a different
pair of its own, so each looked like it covered the other. The list is
read off `src/actaira` now and CI calls the script instead of repeating
it.

CI also runs the published Action on this repository's own pushes and
uploads the result to code scanning. The README told a reader that was
theirs to do while this repository did not do it.

DEF-130.
1a9ff0b0:
Execute the Action's shell in the suite

Three defects in three pushes, all in the seam between this repository
and a GitHub Actions runner. That is a hole in the gate rather than three
bugs: `make all` on a clean clone runs no runner, so nothing in it could
have reached any of them, and the only thing standing between the next
push and a fourth was the memory of these three.

`tests/test_action_yml.py` extracts every `run:` body out of `action.yml`
and executes it under `bash -e`, the shell GitHub gives a composite step,
with a stub `actaira` on PATH that exits with whatever code the test
asks for. What it asserts is the direction that broke: that a non-zero
exit is recorded and passed through rather than swallowed.
206e7d80:
Make the Action's own CI job run: two defects only a runner could find

The Action's self-test shipped prepared and undemonstrated, and said so.
The first push demonstrated it in the honest direction: both new jobs
went red, and neither failure was reachable from a laptop.

`python -m zizmor` is not how zizmor is invoked. It is a Rust binary
distributed through PyPI, so `pip install` puts an executable on PATH and
no importable module, and every local run had called it by path. It is
pinned now as well.

The second was the composite action's outputs, which a failed step does
not map, so the job read an empty string in the one case it existed for.
20fa90d3:
Say what changed, sign what it was, and put it where the change arrives

`check` answers what my agents can do here. What this is for is what
CHANGED, in the place the change enters: the pull request. `diff` is that
answer, `seal` signs what the answer was so an approval can expire by
itself, and the GitHub Action is the two of them where somebody will meet
them. Seven commands of seven, with no promised name left.

`diff` reads both trees with `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file` and checks
out neither, so a `post-checkout` hook in the repository being examined
never gets the chance to run.

`attest/package.py::write_package` was reachable only from the suite, so
there was a verifier of a format nothing produced. `seal` is the producer.
275ecf40:
Run the gate with make, and measure two holes it does not cover

`make all` had never been executed: the four steps were run by hand,
which proves the four commands and not the Makefile. It runs green under
GNU Make 4.3. No recipe carries a `-` prefix, a `|| true`, a `; true`,
`.IGNORE` or `$(MAKE) -i`.

The changelog states the major as a decision with its reason rather than
leaving it to be inferred from a version bump. The backlog gets the
thirteen README lines per language that state a figure no command
measures any more: the figure check is green because those figures left
the contract, not because the pages are right, and the entry says so.
318bb956:
The README's own example told you to do what ACT-S003 flags

Both `uses:` lines in the documentation pinned a mutable tag. ACT-S003 is
the rule that tells other people a name moves and an approval belongs on
a digest, so an example writing `@main` was this tool asking of a reader
what it flags in their repository.

Both are commit SHAs now, with the command that re-resolves one written
beside them.
3d33c6e0:
DEF-120: ACT-S007 fired on `dontAsk`, which is a repository locking down

The rule named three of the seven values the vendor publishes for
`permissions.defaultMode`, and the resolver knew two. Anything else came
out as the dangerous one, so a repository that had set the strictest mode
available was reported as having widened.

Two greps of our own constants came back short before the vendor's own
reference was read against what this tree does with the key. A set of
values is a fact about somebody else's software, and a grep of our code
can only ever return what we already knew.
3e4363b5:
Demonstrate the two points the Action's defect had taken back

The Action's self-test was signed off as prepared and not demonstrated,
because nothing on a laptop runs a GitHub Actions runner. DEF-123 then
took it away entirely: the job exercised `from-dir`, the branch a
stranger never writes, while the only documented one had never executed.

Both run now. The job runs both branches, and the refs branch is the one
the documentation describes, so a stranger's path is the path that is
tested. The resolver is also run over four real repositories rather than
over fixtures alone.
3faae4e1:
Split the 2,023-line resolver, and move the governance into docs/PRINCIPLES.md

`surface/resolve.py` held three jobs and seven vendors. The citation
table is `merge.py`, the functions that record a capability are
`emit.py`, and the six resolvers that are not Claude Code sit beside the
readers they belong to. Claude Code stays because `claude_code.py` is
imported at module level and moving it would make that import circular.

`test_capability_coverage.py` read `resolve.py` alone, so six resolvers
leaving it would have shrunk the set it checks with nothing going red. It
reads the package now.

The governance is `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`, in English.
40953a7b:
Write down an authorisation that had only ever been agreed out loud

The previous piece of work closed at 17 authored files against a declared
limit of 14. The extension was agreed three times in conversation, with a
reason each time, and none of it reached the repository, so the review
that verified it afterwards read 21 changed files against a written 14
and reported the gate breached. It was not breached. The record was
missing.

The rule that closes it: an authorisation to widen a limit or a scope
goes in the commit message, with the number, the reason and which files
consume it. The repository is the only record that lasts.
487eae96:
DEF-123: the Action's documented path had never worked

A stranger does not pass `from-dir`. A stranger writes `on: pull_request`
and passes nothing, and that path builds a different argv, one with a
`--` in it. `--sarif` was appended after `"$@"`, so it landed after the
separator, argparse read it as two more refs and `diff` exited 2. On
every pull request. Always.

The CI job named "the Action used the way a stranger would" was
exercising the way a stranger would not. It runs both branches now, and
three real pull requests are what found this.
4d91d27a:
Read the other six vendors, and never merge two into one

One vendor answered "what can an agent do here" for one agent. A team
does not use one agent, so until now the product was a Claude Code
linter. `check` reads Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, the VS
Code task and settings files, `devcontainer.json` and the AGENTS.md /
CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md instruction files.

Seven readers, seven merge tables, and a surface that is the UNION of
them rather than a merge. Their precedence ladders disagree: Claude Code
puts the user's file above the project's, Gemini CLI the other way, and
VS Code puts the workspace above both. Two vendors configuring the same
MCP server stay two capabilities with the same digest, each naming its
own file and its own rule, rather than one row belonging to neither.
572f86fe:
Strictness is an invariant, and the verdict fails by default

Supplying a trust anchor is an assertion about what the verifier accepts.
It may turn an OK into a FAILED, which is the point of supplying one, and
it must never do the reverse. It did, twice: an unreadable
`--tsa-trust-store` returned before the RFC 3161 check was recorded, and
a `--trusted-keyring` naming the signing key made a package's own
`status: revoked` unreachable, so `--require-trust` exited 0 on it. Both
printed `Result: OK` on a package that had failed without the flag.

Repairing the two call sites was rejected: neither bug is visible from
inside a test about one argument, because both live between two. The
property is asserted over a corpus of flag combinations instead, and the
verdict now starts FAILED and is earned rather than assumed.
635532f4:
Read what an agent recorded, record it from outside, serve both

One trace document, two sources, and a capture level on every event that
decides what the document is allowed to claim.

Completeness is the invariant: a trace is complete only when something
recorded that it ended AND nothing recorded a hole. A recorder nobody
closed produces an incomplete trace, not an empty clean one. Every
failure path in both transports ends at `Recorder.gap` rather than at a
`return`, and the guard is a property over a corpus of seven ways to lose
an event rather than seven tests that can drift apart. The corpus carries
a healthy case too, because a property test where everything fails would
pass against a proxy that declared a gap on every session.
66b7b9be:
Identity instead of position, and a capture that fails closed

Thirteen findings from an external review, six of them of the worst
class: a false datum recorded as observed. This closes the ones on the
path of `scan`, the privacy ones and the gate.

`rewrite_config` wrote down every server it could not interpose on and
nothing read it back, so a run in which the agent talked to an HTTP
server directly produced a record saying complete, authenticity
established, no gaps. The hole was on disk, one directory away from the
document denying it. `interposition.json` is written every time and read
back now: a server not interposed on is a hole, a server interposed on
with no record is a hole, and no manifest at all is the biggest of the
three.
7a37991f:
Change the subject from what an agent did to what an agent can do

No version is released here. The doctrine is written before the code,
because the repository is the only thing the next person can read, and
each part of it is written so that a check can hold it rather than a
reader.

The governance document goes from nine files to eighteen, in three steps
with the same reason each time: a published file was describing a product
this tree does not have, and this change exists so that the repository
stops doing that before the code arrives.
86689e62:
Retire pivot/agent-conformance, and say where the product line lives

`main` is the product line from here on. It went to the remote as a
fast-forward over an ancestor, so nothing was rewritten and nothing lost.

`pivot/agent-conformance` sat two phases behind, at a commit that is in
`main`'s own history, so it held nothing unpublished. A branch that
duplicates the main line and then falls behind it is a branch somebody
starts from without noticing.

The backlog line saying main was unpublished is struck where it stood
rather than deleted: it was true, and a closed entry is evidence that the
thing closed.
8e0285fb:
Put the gates where a machine runs them, and write the layering down

`release-check` and a re-measurement of the figures are CI jobs now. They
could not be before: `figures.py` wrote a wall clock and the current HEAD
into its own output, so two runs over one tree never agreed and
`git diff --exit-code` could not mean anything.

`tests/test_layering.py` says what each package may import, as an
allowlist of edges: a prohibition list is silent about the package nobody
thought of. `make all` runs the suite with a coverage floor of 88 against
a measured 90, and two checks arrive: a fixture nothing reads, and a make
target a document names that does not exist. That found six on one page.
DEF-128, DEF-129.
93363ce9:
Backlog: what `uses: $/` resolves to on a pull request is not known

It is documented as the workflow's own repository, and what that means
for a pull request from a fork is not something this repository has
observed. Written down rather than assumed, because the difference
decides whether a fork's own Action file could run.
95e21ab8:
A reference that is one, a protocol with no session, and a dead transport

The previous capture was honest about what it did not see. Three things
made that honesty insufficient.

The redaction was an encoding. `label_ref` published
`server:<sha256(alias)[:16]>`, and the aliases people type come from a
public set of about eight words, so the digest is the same on every
machine that has ever existed. The property meant to catch it seeded
high-entropy secrets, which a reversible digest passes while protecting
nothing. A 128-bit salt per session now, kept out of every document.

The other two: the protocol reader had no notion of a session, and one
transport had never been executed by anything.
9d1476f1:
Inventory the values the resolver reads, with the set each belongs to

This builds nothing, on purpose. What a piece of work opens with is its
criterion, and a criterion written afterwards is a description of the
work.

Why it exists: `surface/gemini.py` knows one constant, so every other
string is "not that one", which is the safe end of the order. The day a
vendor adds a mode wider than every mode we know, an unknown value falls
to that safe end and a real widening comes out NARROWED. That is a false
negative in the one direction where it matters, and it is the same
disease as two earlier defects rather than a Gemini fix.
9d263931:
DEF-122: a figures pattern that matched nothing was skipped in silence

A figure that declares a page and matches nothing in it used to
`continue`. Four sat unguarded that way, two of them stale, under a
paragraph claiming all four were measured and gate-refused.

The test beside it held the defect in place. It asserted
`f"**{value}**" in page`, and bold between a figure and the noun it
counts is exactly what makes the figure invisible to the pattern. Both
green, the published figure off by eight.

Declared and absent is a contradiction and the only honest answer is red.
The bilingual check had the same shape: it passed because the figure was
missing from both languages.
9d95fefb:
DEF-119: rotating a key could leave the retired one an inverted window

A rotation wrote the retired key's `not_after` from the clock and its
`not_before` from the record, and on a key created and rotated inside the
same second the two came out the wrong way round. Every signature that
key had ever made then verified against a window that contained nothing.

The window is derived from the record on both ends now, and the twin test
rotates twice inside one second and demands the old signatures still
verify.
aacf635c:
Publish two more limits: what Windows cannot show, and what the proxy will not invent

`watch` works on Windows: the healthy path is indistinguishable from
Linux's. What is not is a server that closes its transport while still
running, because the operating system does not deliver EOF to the reader
while the writing process is alive. The gap comes out `upstream_timeout`
and not `transport_closed`. The run is recorded and the gap is declared
either way; what is lost is which of the two happened.

The second: when an upstream produces no reply, the proxy records the gap
and forwards nothing, so a client with no deadline of its own waits.
Writing a timeout error back would put a message in the agent's own input
that no server sent, and the agent could not tell it from a real one.
b5d29a4e:
Run the gate on the tree that is published, not on the one that is here

The previous commit went green on this machine and red on CI, and the two
are the same commit. The difference was two fixture files that exist on
this disk and are not in the repository: `.gitignore` excludes `.vscode/`
everywhere, `git add -A` skipped both without a word, and every test that
reads them was answering about this laptop.

That matters more than a missing file. `.vscode/tasks.json` is half of
the attack those fixtures are about, and the test asserting exactly that
passed over a tree where the file was present and unpublishable.

The gate runs on a clean clone of HEAD from here on, and
`tests/test_fixtures_are_published.py` asserts the specific case.
50e6f81a:
Pin the screenshot fixture's clocks, so regenerating is not a diff

The demo story is built by the commands an operator types, which is the
point. What it inherited was `datetime.now()` in every row, so two runs
of `make screenshots` produced two different pictures of one story and
this repository, which commits its captures, would carry a permanent diff
nobody could read.

The clocks are pinned after the commands have built it, and that is
checked rather than assumed: a snapshot's digest covers the source, the
connector, the revision and the artifacts, and deliberately not
`observed_at`. No identity moves, which is the only reason this is a
fixture helper and not a falsification.
b851ad9c:
The composite step died under `bash -e` before it could record anything

A composite action's `run:` gets `bash -e`, so the first non-zero exit
ends the step. The step captured the tool's exit code on the line after
the call, which never ran, and the file the next step reads was never
written.

The call is guarded and the code captured in the same statement now, and
the suite executes that shell under the same flag rather than reading it.
b88548a4:
Say what an agent can do here, and cite the rule that settled it

`actaira check` reads Claude Code's configuration out of a repository,
resolves what it actually permits across scopes, and applies fifteen
rules that each name their author. It executes nothing it reads, prints
no literal without being asked, and answers INDETERMINATE rather than
guessing.

Both 2026 npm worms are reconstructed as fixtures with their citations:
`mini-shai-hulud/` is the settings file StepSecurity and Mend publish
verbatim, `keyv-august/` is rebuilt from the sentences Snyk, Aikido and
Wiz published. The scripts they point at are inert stubs. A security
repository that shipped the worm's payload to demonstrate catching the
worm would be the worm.
bba54033:
Use `uses: $/` for the Action self-test, now the job has been green twice

GitHub's self-repository syntax is stricter than `./`: it cannot load an
action a previous step cloned at runtime, and it counts as pinning for
policy enforcement.

It arrives in a commit of its own, after the job had already been green
twice with `./`, so a red build here can only be about this one line. The
Action and this syntax were both unverified at once and a failure would
not have said which.
bf6493dd:
Two views of what the resolver decides on, compared over pairs

A correct total and two agreeing views can coexist with a lost key and a
phantom site. Thirteen keys, both views agreeing, one key gone and its
decision credited to another.

`_sandbox` binds `entry` twice, once for `excludedCommands` and once for
`allowedDomains`. The reader kept one mark per name per function, last
writer winning, so the first vanished and the second reported a site it
never had. Nothing was red.

Every binding of a name opens a new mark now, and the comparison between
the views is over pairs of key and line rather than over sets of keys.
c0a33675:
DEF-124: the fix for DEF-123 moved a quote, and no laptop reads that shell

The commit that fixed DEF-123 inserted three steps into the `action` job
above the line that closed a `python -c "` string, so the closing quote
ended up inside a later step. Two steps were unparseable shell and the
job died before reaching the branch that commit existed to add.

The YAML stayed valid, so every reader that reads YAML stayed happy:
zizmor passed, `make all` passed, the suite passed.
`tests/test_action_yml.py` exists for shell embedded in YAML and does not
read `.github/workflows/` at all, so a check built for exactly this seam
covered one of the two files that have it.

`tests/test_workflow_shell.py` now hands every embedded shell to `bash -n`.
c328590f:
DEF-121: a gap test red on Windows, green in the gate, and no way to say so

The ledger could record that a defect was fixed and could not record that
one was open, so a defect found on a machine the gate does not run on had
nowhere to live except a sentence somebody would have to remember.

`fixed` is a field now and the count of what is still open is a measured
figure like every other, which means the page that states it cannot
quietly say "all fixed" again.
70a5ec90:
Add the evidence explorer, change timeline and validity panels

Both panels are readers over the same engine functions the CLI calls,
behind the same Host and Origin checks as the graph routes, against a
workspace chosen when the server starts and never named by a request.

The evidence panel puts the digest a record was taken about beside the
digest its subject has now, and beside a third value saying whether the
subject is in the latest observation at all. Without that third value an
artifact removed from its source shows two equal digests next to a
superseded badge, which reads as "nothing changed".
cfe8eacd:
Cut the README down and give it two pictures it can regenerate

From 626 lines to 476, with nothing deleted: the published limits move to
their own pages and the four commands that are not `check` or `diff` move
to a commands reference. Every check that read the moved content follows
it, because a claim that leaves the checked set is not moved, it is
unchecked.

The demo picture is an SVG drawn from the command's own output, one per
language, and the gate redraws it and refuses a difference. A GIF is a
binary nothing here could compare against the tool. The licence check
compared by substring, and "LIMITS" contains "MIT". DEF-131.
e13b1bcb:
Every published field says who wrote its value

The server alias, the absolute path in a gap's detail and `requestState`
were one defect found three times. Two were fixed with a salt. The third
was fixed by restricting which CHARACTERS the value may contain, which is
a worse fix: the specification has servers encode their own identifier
there, so a server that put something meaningful in it published it
through a gate that was only looking at punctuation.

So every field of the published trace is classified in one place, with
who writes its value. Fifty-one fields: twenty-nine written by this tool,
twenty-two by an agent, a server or somebody else's configuration, and
three named and deliberately not read at all.
e6fddf61:
Prepare the history rewrite, and leave applying it a deliberate act

Forty-four commit messages, in .github/history-rewrite/messages.json. The
history reads as a work log: fourteen bodies over a hundred lines,
the longest 449, with phase numbers and file limits in them. What those
bodies argued is in docs/DESIGN.md, docs/defects.json and CHANGELOG.md,
where a reader finds it without running git log.

replay.py rebuilds the branch with them. It replays each commit's recorded
tree object rather than applying patches, so the final tree is identical by
construction, and it carries the author and committer dates over untouched.
Without --apply it moves nothing: a rewrite of a published branch is
somebody's decision, and the runbook has the rest.
ec7001f6:
Backlog: the three lines the value inventory is opened against

Three places where an unknown value falls to the safe end of an order
rather than being declared unknown. Written down before the work starts,
so the criterion is not a description of what was done.
f7065270:
3.0.0: archive the model scanner, keep the evidence core

The subject becomes AI agent runs. formats, controls, connectors, scan,
bom, agents, governance, web, evals_support and nine loose modules are
archived whole at v2.3.0. attest, state, report, policy, receipt, model,
miniyaml and manifest survive.

Two cryptographic defects fixed on the way out. The chain entry hash
promised length prefixes and joined six fields with "|", and a
demonstrated collision moved "deadbeef|" across a field boundary without
changing the digest. The package manifest and the receipt both signed 32
bare bytes under one key, so a signature made in one role verified in the
other. Each has a constant domain prefix now, both pinned by tests.
f7fa019c:
Take out what was dead and say what the line count measures

The orphan CycloneDX schema (262 KB, referenced nowhere), ten
per-file-ignores for modules deleted a release ago, and two MANIFEST.in
prune lines for directories that went to v2.3.0. Ruff and setuptools both
answer a miss with silence, so the gate reads both files through one
definition now and refuses a path that is not there.

Both READMEs published the size of the tree as if it were the size of the
product. Both figures are stated now, each on its own noun. Fixing that
rewrapped a paragraph and unhooked a figure from the pattern that keeps
it current, which is how the markup guard turned out to have been reading
a hand-typed noun list that never contained `lines`. DEF-125 to DEF-127.
f83125b8:
Write down three rules the tree already followed

None of the three is new scope; all three are already true of the tree
and already have their cases. What they did not have is a place the next
person can read them from.

A test that proves a negative carries a twin that plants the case and
demands the failure. Two checks over one property share their definition,
or they cancel: each passes on its own terms and the failure hides
between them. A check that does not match, does not find or does not
apply fails loudly and names what it was looking for, rather than writing
zero or falling to the safe end.
c9ad00aa:
A path assertion that was a no-op on Windows

It compared the plain spelling of a path against a JSON body. On Windows
a backslash is doubled on the wire, so the substring never matched and
the assertion could not fail: a real check on Linux and a no-op on the
machine it was written on.

CI found what it was for. The test also asserted something broader than
the property. A source URI the operator registered IS an absolute path
and is the identity of the source. The assertion is about the database's
path specifically now, in both spellings, and states separately that the
source URI is disclosed and why that is right.

No production code changed: nothing was leaking the database path.
2647168b:
Wire the evidence loop: producers, change propagation, validity

The ledger declared seven kinds of evidence and only `watch` ever wrote
one, so three of them were vocabulary rather than data. `scan`,
`agent check` and `policy check` file theirs now, all behind `--state`:
no flag, no workspace, no change in behaviour.

Identity comes from the workspace and is never invented. Evidence binds
to an asset the store already records, found by scanned digest or by a
declared handle, and a subject nothing has observed records nothing and
says why. `artifact:<basename>` would have been evidence about whichever
model.pt was scanned last.
